the Great American Biotical Interchange (GABI) was the result of a complex interplay of tectonics, sea level changes, climate and holding pens.

the role of tectonics, climate, sea level changes, vegetation changes, and dispersal corridors in the biotic dynamics of South America.

the biogeography of mammals in North America, South America, and Central America, with special emphasis on the biogeography and phylogenetic relationships of the families Canidae and Felidae.

the Great American Botic Interchange was the result of the combined effects of the tectonic opening of the Isthmus of Panama, the development of a tropical rainforest, and the development of non-tropical ecologic communities.
the Great American Botic Interchange was the result of multiple, complex and dynamic processes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Great American Biotical Interchange is a product of tectonics, climate, sea level and holding pens.
the Great American Biotical Interchange is a product of the tectonic and climatic dynamics of the last 25 million years.
the Great American Biotical Interchange is a complex and multifaceted process, involving multiple dispersals, multiple holding pens and multiple tectonic events.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the biotic dynamics of the Great Interchange are not as straightforward as they are often presented.
the biotic exchanges between North and South America were more complex, dynamic, and temporally variable than previously thought.

the biogeographic patterns and processes that have been observed in the Neotropics over the last 20 million years are the result of the complex interaction of tectonics, climate, and biota, and not simply the result of the development of the Isthmus of Panama.
